transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's just that I've been having this... well, I guess you could call it a little habit, and it's getting a bit embarrassing. 

I just sort of keep getting up when I'm really supposed to stay put. Like, I'll be right in the middle of a client interview—I'm a private investigator, by the way—or doing a tutoring session, or even just sitting with the ladies at my book club. It's not that I don't care about what anyone is saying! I just have this urge to move around. But, um, people are starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen like everyone else does, and I don't want them to think I'm being rude. 

I hope that's the kind of thing you can help with? Am I explaining that okay?
How long have you been experiencing this urge to get up and move around?

Well, I mean, I've always been a bit... energetic, I suppose. But it hasn't really been an issue until somewhat recently. 

I'd say it's been noticeably worse for about, oh, maybe eight months? Right around the time I had to move out of my old apartment in Chicago. It was a bit of a stressful transition, and I guess my nerves just got a little frayed. I'm sure it's probably just stress making me a little restless, right? Does that timeline make sense to you?
Are you currently taking any prescription medications?

Oh, no, I'm not. No prescriptions at all right now. I, um... I usually try to just manage things on my own, you know? Just to stay healthy and not be a bother to anyone. 

So, no, no medications. I hope that makes things a little easier for you to figure out? I know sometimes pills can complicate things, so... hopefully that's a good thing?

{"intent": "Assess for inattention symptoms to differentiate between ADHD combined presentation, ADHD hyperactive/impulsive presentation, and other conditions", "question": "Outside of feeling restless, do you often find

Find it hard to concentrate, you mean? Oh, no, not at all. I'm actually very good at paying attention. I mean, with my line of work, I really have to be, right? 

I don't lose focus or forget what people are saying, and I'm always very tuned in to my clients or whatever book we're discussing at my club. It's really just... well, my body just wants to be up and moving while my brain is working. But my mind stays right on track. 

So, no, I don't think I have any trouble with my focus or anything like that. I hope that's what you were asking? Did I answer that okay?
{"intent": "Assess if the urge to move is associated with uncomfortable physical sensations in the legs to evaluate for restless legs syndrome", "question": "When you feel that urge to move, do

Do I feel anything in my legs? Like, a weird sensation? Oh, um, no, not really. It's not like an ache or a creep-crawly feeling or anything uncomfortable like that. 

It's more just... a general energy, you know? Like my body just has a little too much pep and wants to be doing something. It's not painful or bothersome in a physical way. I just... I just like to be on the go. 

So, no weird feelings in my legs. I hope that's a good sign? That means it's probably nothing too serious, right?

Did I have a lot of energy back then, too? Um... yes, I suppose I did. I mean, I was a very happy, active kid! 

My mother still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through, just investigating everything. And, um, my grade-school report cards... well, they always said I was very bright! But they also usually mentioned that I couldn't really stay in my seat or wait my turn very well. 

I was just so eager to participate, you know? I didn't mean to be disruptive or anything. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid? I really did try to be good!
